subject.title: fix(discord): sustained gateway bursts stop growing memory

question: Should ordinary Discord Gateway sends reject synchronously after one 120-event queued window, or should particular stale/idempotent event types receive a coalescing policy instead?
rationale: The patch eliminates unbounded memory growth, but its visible failure mode during sustained overload is a deliberate channel-behavior decision rather than a purely mechanical correction.

options.title: Confirm bounded rejection
options.body: Accept one additional 120-event window and explicit rejection thereafter, preserving the proposed caller containment and critical-send bypass.

options.title: Design event-aware coalescing
options.body: Pause this branch and define which idempotent Gateway events may replace queued state instead of failing under overload.

recommendation.title: Confirm bounded rejection
recommendation.body: Accept one additional 120-event window and explicit rejection thereafter, preserving the proposed caller containment and critical-send bypass.
